content.value_statement: Survival modeling requires methods that handle censored time-to-event data. This skill guides scikit-survival workflows from data preparation through model evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to prepare structured survival outcomes with scikit-survival utilities.
Guides selection between Cox models, ensemble models, Survival SVMs, and non-parametric estimators.
Shows how to evaluate predictions with concordance index, time-dependent AUC, and Brier score.
Covers preprocessing needs for censored datasets, including encoding, scaling, and missing values.
Provides guidance for competing risks and cumulative incidence analysis.
limitations: Does not run analyses or validate results without a user-provided Python environment and dataset.
Does not replace statistical review for clinical, legal, or regulatory decisions.
Focuses on scikit-survival and may not cover every survival analysis package.
Example workflows require adaptation for each study design and censoring pattern.

use_cases.title: Prepare censored datasets
use_cases.description: Convert event and time columns into scikit-survival format and plan preprocessing for reliable modeling.

use_cases.title: Compare survival model families
use_cases.description: Choose between interpretable Cox models, ensemble methods, and Survival SVMs for a project goal.

use_cases.title: Review survival model evaluation
use_cases.description: Select metrics that account for censoring and explain concordance, calibration, and time-dependent discrimination.

prompt_templates.title: Start a survival workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a scikit-survival workflow for a dataset with event, time, and clinical feature columns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CoxPHSurvivalAnalysis, RandomSurvivalForest, GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis, and Survival SVM for my dataset and goals.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate predictions
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend survival model evaluation metrics for my censoring rate, prediction horizon, and available train-test split.

prompt_templates.title: Design competing risks analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis with multiple event types
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a competing risks analysis with cumulative incidence functions and cause-specific interpretation for my event categories.

output_examples.input: I have time, event, age, treatment, and biomarker columns. What should I do first?
output: Check that event indicators and times are valid, then create a structured survival outcome.
Encode categorical features, impute missing values, and split data while monitoring censoring rates.
Start with an interpretable Cox model before comparing more flexible models.

output_examples.input: My censoring rate is high. Which concordance metric should I report?
output_examples.output: Use Uno's concordance index when censoring is moderate or high, and report the censoring rate with the metric.

output_examples.input: I need probabilities for different causes of failure.
output_examples.output: Use competing risks methods and estimate cumulative incidence for each event type instead of treating other causes as simple censoring.

best_practices: Validate event indicators, time values, and censoring rates before fitting any model.
Use scaling for SVMs and regularized Cox models, preferably inside a pipeline.
Report more than one metric when comparing survival models.
anti_patterns: Do not treat competing events as ordinary censoring when event type probabilities matter.
Do not use Harrell's concordance index alone when censoring is high.
Do not tune models on test data or compare models without consistent evaluation splits.

faq.question: What is scikit-survival used for?
faq.answer: It is used for survival analysis and time-to-event modeling with censored data in Python.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete analysis code?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and example patterns, but users must adapt them to their data and environment.

faq.question: Which models does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Cox models, penalized Cox models, ensemble survival models, Survival SVMs, and non-parametric estimators.

faq.question: Can it help with competing risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cumulative incidence functions and when competing risks methods are appropriate.

faq.question: What metrics are included?
faq.answer: It covers concordance index, time-dependent AUC, Brier score, and integrated Brier score.

faq.question: Is this a medical decision tool?
faq.answer: No. It supports technical analysis workflows and does not replace expert statistical or clinical review.
